findings.title: ClickHouse users store plaintext-recoverable passwords, the audit runs as a full-admin account, and the endpoint is non-TLS
findings.impact: Plaintext passwords are recoverable by anyone who can read ClickHouse config or system tables, and an audit/read path that holds INSERT/ALTER/DROP/SYSTEM grants can mutate or destroy telemetry by accident or if compromised. Over an untrusted network the non-TLS endpoint would also expose credentials in transit.

evidence.check: Service users are not on plaintext_password
evidence.command: clickhouse-client --query "SELECT name, auth_type, host_ip FROM system.users ORDER BY name FORMAT TabSeparatedWithNames"
evidence.observed: api	['plaintext_password']	['::/0'] ; default	['plaintext_password']	[] ; worker	['plaintext_password']	['::/0'] — all 3 users use plaintext_password (hardened forms are sha256_password / double_sha1_password)

evidence.check: External default user requires a password (unauthenticated probe; status code is the evidence)
evidence.observed: 401 — body: 'Code: 194. DB::Exception: default: Authentication failed: password is incorrect, or there is no user with such name'. Good: the default user is NOT open. But its stored auth_type is still plaintext_password.

evidence.check: The audit/read credential is least-privilege (SELECT/SHOW only)
evidence.observed: GRANT CHECK, SHOW, SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE, DROP, UNDROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, OPTIMIZE, BACKUP, KILL QUERY, SYSTEM, ... ON *.* TO default — the account used to read holds full DDL/DML/admin grants; no scoped read-only user exists for audits.

evidence.command: printf '%s' "$CH_URL" | grep -qE '^https://' && echo https || echo plaintext
evidence.observed: plaintext http endpoint (:8123). Host class here is loopback in this POC, so in-transit exposure is limited today; a non-loopback deployment on plaintext http is a transport-security gap.

findings.recommendation: Move the api, worker, and default users off plaintext_password to sha256_password. Create a dedicated read-only ClickHouse user (SELECT on the telemetry database + system.*) for audits instead of reading as the full-admin default. Terminate a TLS listener and point audit traffic at https for any non-loopback path.

findings.title: The storefront application services emit logs and traces but no metrics
findings.impact: With no per-service metrics, there is no dashboardable throughput/latency/resource time series and no metric-threshold alerting for the storefront services; responders must reconstruct rates and saturation from raw traces/logs during an incident. The metrics pipeline itself is healthy (the collector's own metrics land and are fresh), so this is a service-instrumentation gap, not a broken pipeline.

evidence.command: clickhouse-client --query "SELECT ServiceName, count() FROM otel_logs WHERE Timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY ServiceName"
evidence.observed: api-gateway=20, payment-service=20, checkout-service=20 — logs present for all 3 services (60 rows total; INFO=46, WARN=8, ERROR=6).

evidence.command: clickhouse-client --query "SELECT ServiceName, count() FROM otel_traces WHERE Timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY ServiceName"
evidence.observed: api-gateway=10, payment-service=10, checkout-service=10 — traces present for all 3 (30 spans; StatusCode ERROR=4; slowest: checkout-service GET /checkout 4200ms STATUS_CODE_ERROR).

evidence.check: Do the storefront services appear in any metrics table?
evidence.command: clickhouse-client --query "SELECT count() FROM otel_metrics_gauge WHERE ServiceName IN ('checkout-service','payment-service','api-gateway')"; plus DISTINCT ServiceName per metrics table
evidence.observed: 0 storefront metric rows. Metrics tables carry only collector self-telemetry: gauge ServiceName = {otelcol, otelcol-hyperdx}, sum/histogram = {otelcol-hyperdx}. The tables are non-empty (gauge 385, sum 213, histogram 16) but hold zero rows for the 3 application services.

findings.recommendation: Instrument checkout-service, payment-service, and api-gateway to emit OpenTelemetry metrics (RED/USE), or configure the OTel collector's metrics pipeline to receive and export their metrics to ClickHouse. If these services are intentionally metrics-free, declare that in business_context.md so the audit records it not-in-scope instead of a gap.

findings.title: HyperDX alerting and dashboards are auth-gated and could not be seen this run (no API key)
findings.impact: Without a HyperDX API key, whether any alert reaches a human (CS-040) and whether dashboards/sources exist for the critical services (CS-041) are unknown — an empty result here would be a can't-see-it gap, never a confident zero. These two categories are excluded from the score and renormalized; the ClickHouse-backed categories remain scored.

evidence.command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<hyperdx>:8080/api/health ; and the same for /api/alerts /api/dashboards /api/sources
evidence.observed: /api/health=200 (HyperDX v2.35.0, env=production) — reachable. /api/alerts=401 (body 'Unauthorized'), /api/dashboards=401, /api/sources=401 — all auth-gated. /api/v1/alerts=404 confirms the base path is /api/<resource>, not /api/v1/*.

evidence.check: Estate-sizing guarded alert fetch does not silently count zero
evidence.observed: curl exit 22 (HTTP 401); the guard printed the WARN path and left the alert count unknown rather than recording 0 — correct handling.

findings.recommendation: Configure a read-only HyperDX API key (clickstack.hyperdx_api_key_env) via /scoutflo:connect and re-run so alerting (CS-040) and dashboards/sources (CS-041) can be scored end to end.
